import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 324

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/324](https://www.erdosproblems.com/324)
-/

open scoped Polynomial

namespace Erdos324

/--
Does there exist a polynomial $f(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that all the sums $f(a)+f(b)$ with
$a < b$ nonnegative integers are distinct?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_324 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ f : ℤ[X], {(a, b) : ℕ × ℕ | a < b}.InjOn fun (a, b) => f.eval (a : ℤ) + f.eval (b : ℤ) := by
  sorry

/--
Probably $f(x) = x^5$ has the property that the sums $f(a)+f(b)$ with
$a < b$ nonnegative integers are distinct.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_324.variants.quintic : {(a, b) : ℕ × ℕ | a < b}.InjOn fun (a, b) => a ^ 5 + b ^ 5 := by
  sorry

end Erdos324

reformulations.difference: The source proposes the integer polynomial f(x)=x^5; Lean directly states injectivity of the natural-number-valued sum a^5+b^5.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Evaluating X^5 over ℤ at the natural-number inputs gives the integer cast of a^5+b^5. Since ℕ → ℤ preserves addition and powers and is injective, equality of outputs—and consequently InjOn on the identical domain a<b—is equivalent in both formulations. This equivalence was proved as Review324.quintic_cast_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Both declarations faithfully match the source, whose explicit question uses nonnegative integers and the strict bound a<b. The source still marks the problem OPEN and proposes x^5, so both status tags agree. Lean checks proved the expansion of InjOn into four-variable uniqueness and ruled out every constant polynomial as a trivial witness; these proofs do not depend on sorryAx. Boundary and finite tests passed, including fifth-power injectivity on inputs below 10 and known collisions for powers 1–4. Both scratch files compile without errors or warnings.
